comparable_cases.why_comparable: A 2019 CUA for Kaleifornia restaurant at 36 West Portal Ave (285 m away, same NCD-WEST PORTAL district). This was a use decision requiring a Planning Commission hearing for a new restaurant, approved with conditions including restrictive hours.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The one recent conditioned approval in the neighborhood imposed strict operating hours of 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily, plus standard eating-and-drinking conditions (trash, noise, odor control, community liaison). This suggests the Commission may condition even non-alcohol restaurant operations if evening activity is proposed, though the current concept's pre-midnight hours are less sensitive.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: A 2015 CUA at 160 West Portal Ave (109 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) approving a change from Limited Restaurant to full Restaurant for Toast Eatery. This is a use decision showing an intensification of food use on the same block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approval to expand from limited to full restaurant service at a nearby address confirms the district supports full-service dining. The absence of extracted conditions suggests a straightforward approval when the use is principally permitted and well-operated.

comparable_cases.address: 170 WEST PORTAL AV, SAN FRANCISCO, CA
comparable_cases.why_comparable: A 2011 CUA at 170 West Portal Ave (109 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) approving a change of use to full-service restaurant (Sweet Orchid). This is a use decision from the Planning Commission for a new full-service restaurant in the same district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Full-service restaurant approved without extracted conditions in the immediate West Portal corridor, reinforcing that the neighborhood supports dining establishments when they comply with zoning and operational standards.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: A 2020 agency referral at 118 West Portal Ave (148 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) for a Limited Restaurant (Shaw's) involving a change of ownership and continuation of existing use. This is an agency referral, not a Commission decision, so it carries less weight but shows recent activity.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning routinely approves continuation and ownership changes for existing restaurant uses via the referral process, demonstrating that restaurant operations are well-established and accepted in the district.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: A 2015 agency referral at 301 West Portal Ave (97 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) for Fuji Restaurant, documenting continuation of an existing restaurant with ABC license that had operated since 1999, with hours until 10:30 p.m. This is an agency referral showing long-standing restaurant operations.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A restaurant with evening hours (closing at 10:30 p.m. weekdays, 10 p.m. weekends) has operated successfully at a nearby address since 1999, indicating the neighborhood tolerates restaurant activity into the evening, well beyond the 8 p.m. limit imposed on Kaleifornia.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain written confirmation from Planning Department whether the proposed 3,995 sq ft restaurant at 243 West Portal Ave requires a Conditional Use Authorization and whether the prior use at this address affects the pathway.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting with Planning's Zoning Administrator or a planner assigned to the West Portal neighborhood. Bring the 2012 agency referral records (MB1200147 and MB1201143) showing prior restaurant approval at 243-255 West Portal Ave. Ask: (1) whether the 2,500+ sq ft size trigger applies to this specific site given the prior use, (2) what the records show as the last use of the space, and (3) whether the concept as described requires a CUA or can proceed with over-the-counter zoning review. timeline_cost.notes: The 120-300 day range and $5,200-$24,000 government cost range are the time and fees to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (if required) and Health Permit to Operate. This is a time to approval, not a time to denial or withdrawal. The range assumes: (1) a CUA is required for the 3,995 sq ft size and takes 120-180 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing plus 30-day appeal period (typical CUA fee range $3,100-$15,000 depending on construction cost, with First Year Free waivers available for new storefront businesses); (2) health plan check takes 21-60 days ($828-$2,500, catalog:sf.health_plan_check) and the Health Permit to Operate takes 14-45 days ($470-$1,000, catalog:sf.health_permit) after construction is complete. If Planning confirms no CUA is required (e.g., the prior restaurant use at this address continues or the size trigger is waived), the timeline collapses to 35-105 days (health plan check plus permit to operate plus business registration) and government costs drop to $1,400-$3,700. Government costs shown exclude: building permit fees (a percentage of construction valuation, $800-$15,000 estimated, catalog:sf.building_permit), Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446-$1,500, catalog:sf.fire_place_of_assembly), sign permit ($300-$1,500, catalog:sf.sign_permit), state entity registration ($70-$150, catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), business registration ($55-$700, catalog:sf.business_registration), FBN filing ($60-$120, catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), food safety certifications ($107-$265 total, catalog:ca.food_safety_manager_cert and catalog:ca.food_handler_card for 20 employees), music licenses ($600-$5,000/year, catalog:us.ascap_license and catalog:us.bmi_license), and workers' compensation insurance premiums (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). Construction duration (storefront merger, kitchen build-out) is not included in this timeline; it runs in parallel with or after the CUA hearing and adds 2-6 months to the overall project schedule. The critical path item is confirming with Planning whether a CUA is required; that answer determines whether the timeline is 3-5 months (no CUA) or 6-10 months (CUA required).

The site history shows two 2012 Planning approvals for restaurant use with a Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine), indicating this address has operated as a restaurant.
